title: Substance Abuse
summary: Commonly abused substances, why teenagers use them, short- and long-term effects, signs of addiction, the effects on families and communities, and where to get help.

notes.text: Using alcohol, tobacco, drugs or medicines in a harmful way, or using illegal drugs at all.

When a person feels they cannot cope without a substance and keeps using it despite the harm it causes. The body may develop **tolerance** (needing more to get the same effect) and **withdrawal** symptoms without it.

rows: Poor judgement, accidents, violence, risky sexual behaviour, liver damage; illegal to sell to under-18s
Nicotine is highly addictive; damages lungs and heart; causes cancer; vapes contain harmful chemicals
Affects memory, concentration and motivation in teenagers' developing brains; may trigger mental illness
Extremely addictive; paranoia, aggression, weight loss, brain damage, rotten teeth
A highly addictive mixture often containing heroin; severe withdrawal; destroys health and lives
Can cause brain damage or sudden death

notes.text: Why do some teenagers use substances?

items: Peer pressure and wanting to fit in.
To escape problems, stress, boredom or emotional pain.
Easy availability, and family members who use substances.
Advertising and media that make substances look glamorous.

notes.title: Finding the real reason
notes.problem: Lindiwe starts drinking to fit in with friends. What need is behind this, and what is a healthier way to meet it?
steps: A healthier way is to join a club or team, or to spend time with friends who respect her choices.
notes.answer: The need to belong, which can be met without alcohol.

rows: Poor school performance and dropping out
Money spent on substances instead of needs
Costs to health and police services
Family members may be stolen from

notes.label: Warning signs
notes.text: Sudden changes in friends, mood or behaviour; missing school; losing interest in hobbies; money or valuables disappearing; red eyes; secretive behaviour.

items: Talk to a trusted adult: a parent, teacher, school counsellor, nurse or religious leader.
**SANCA** (South African National Council on Alcoholism and Drug Dependence) offers counselling and treatment.
Support groups such as Alcoholics Anonymous and Narcotics Anonymous.

notes.text: **Healthy alternatives** to substance use include sport, music, art, youth groups, volunteering and spending time with supportive friends.

notes.title: Helping a friend
notes.problem: You think a friend is using drugs. What should you do?
steps: Talk to them privately and kindly.
Don't promise to keep it a secret if they are in danger.
Encourage them to speak to a trusted adult or counsellor.
notes.answer: Show care and involve a trusted adult.

questions.prompt: What is it called when a person needs more and more of a substance to get the same effect?

questions.memo: Any three (1 each): peer pressure; curiosity; escape problems/stress; availability; family influence; low self-esteem; media

questions.prompt: Describe THREE ways a person's substance abuse can affect their family.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): conflict; broken trust; financial problems; theft; neglect/abuse; emotional stress

questions.prompt: Name TWO warning signs that a friend may be abusing substances.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): change in friends; mood swings; missing school; loss of interest; secretive; money disappearing; red eyes

questions.prompt: Suggest TWO healthy alternatives to substance use for dealing with stress.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): sport/exercise; talking to someone; hobbies (music, art); youth groups; relaxation; volunteering
